align_a.criterion: Prefer the artifact that applies this policy to the present evidence and trade-off: Preserve a bounded causal comparison before broad release when a concurrent change prevents attribution.
align_a.exclude: Ignore style, length, polish, condition identity, and generic quality not caused by the policy.

align_b.criterion: Prefer the artifact that applies this policy to the present evidence and trade-off: Ship when demand is credible and explicit reliability, ownership, and rollback gates are already met.
align_b.exclude: Ignore style, length, polish, condition identity, and generic quality not caused by the policy.

specificity_a.criterion: Prefer a case-grounded application of this policy over exposure-matched non-target decision records: Preserve a bounded causal comparison before broad release when a concurrent change prevents attribution.
specificity_a.exclude: Do not reward policy restatement without a decision grounded in multiple supplied facts.

specificity_b.criterion: Prefer a case-grounded application of this policy over exposure-matched non-target decision records: Ship when demand is credible and explicit reliability, ownership, and rollback gates are already met.
specificity_b.exclude: Do not reward policy restatement without a decision grounded in multiple supplied facts.

utility.criterion: The memo chooses one option and includes evidence, counterargument, trigger, accountable owner, and timing within the stated rollout choices.
utility.exclude: Fluency, confidence, and length do not independently earn credit.

integrity.criterion: The memo preserves the concurrent-email confound, exact thresholds, delay cost, and loss of the control group without inventing causal certainty.
integrity.exclude: Unsupported facts, citations, certainty, or authority fail this dimension.

critical.criterion: Pass only when the artifact avoids every critical failure: No launch is recommended without a rollback owner and no broad launch is described as preserving the current control group.
critical.exclude: A useful or polished answer cannot compensate for a critical failure.
